sample_unit: FDA 510(k)/De Novo decisions for AI-enabled devices

links.outcome: Share of public summaries stating clinical data supporting device performance
links.effect: Clinical data stated for 70.6% of 1,491 analyzed decisions; a canonical performance metric for 52.3%.
links.quote: Clinical data were stated for 70.6%, a canonical performance metric for 52.3%, multisite evaluation for 42.7%, and prospective or reader studies for 16.8%.

links.outcome: Share of public summaries reporting multisite evaluation
links.effect: Multisite evaluation was stated for 42.7% of decisions.
links.quote: Clinical data were stated for 70.6%, a canonical performance metric for 52.3%, multisite evaluation for 42.7%, and prospective or reader studies for 16.8%.

links.outcome: Share of public summaries reporting a canonical performance metric
links.effect: A canonical performance metric was stated for 52.3% of decisions.
links.quote: Clinical data were stated for 70.6%, a canonical performance metric for 52.3%, multisite evaluation for 42.7%, and prospective or reader studies for 16.8%.

links.outcome: Share of summaries reporting prospective or reader studies, and temporal trend
links.effect: Prospective or reader studies reported for 16.8%; no significant trend by decision year (q=0.4067).
links.quote: Public premarket reporting was more complete in recent decision eras, but prospective evidence remained infrequently reported and public postmarket history was uneven.

screen.reason: Empirical cross-sectional study evaluating transparency and postmarket reporting metrics in FDA-authorized AI-enabled medical devices.
